• Input is a string containing only characters from the set {'I','V','X','L','C','D','M'} for valid numerals; invalid
numerals (e.g. 'IIII', 'VV', 'IC', 'IL', 'XD', 'XM', 'VX', 'LC', 'DM', empty string) must be rejected by raising a ValueError.
• The function must reject invalid Roman numerals according to standard subtractive notation rules: only I, X, C can be used
as subtractive prefixes; I can precede V and X only; X can precede L and C only; C can precede D and M only; no more than one
smaller numeral before a larger one; no more than three consecutive identical numerals for I, X, C, M; V, L, D cannot be

• The function is case-sensitive: only uppercase Roman numeral characters are valid; lowercase letters are invalid and must
• The return type is an integer.

this range are invalid and must raise ValueError.
• Whitespace or leading/trailing spaces are not stripped; any whitespace makes the input invalid and must raise ValueError.
